skills.name: Writing monetary amounts in words and figures

note.text: Figures use numerals, while words write an amount in language. When a form includes both, they must express the same amount and currency. Read place value carefully, especially zeros. Check the format requested by the teacher or form; separators and word conventions can vary. The exercise uses invented CFA-franc amounts, not a real payment. Matching words and figures is more important than copying a long number without checking it.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Figures use numerals, while words write an amount in language. When a form includes both, they must express the same amount and currency. Read place value carefully, especially zeros. Check the format requested by the teacher or form; separators and word conventions can vary. The exercise uses invented CFA-franc amounts, not a real payment. Matching words and figures is more important than copying a long number without checking it.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: An imaginary payment form gives the amount as {12500} CFA francs and as {words(12500)} CFA francs. The zeros and place values must agree in both versions. Reading only the first part of the phrase could change the amount. A learner should compare the full expression before signing any classroom model.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Group the amount by place value, write the words and reread them as a number. Keep the currency explicit. Do not add an extra zero or confuse hundreds with thousands. Ask the teacher which accepted number-word style to use in formal examination answers.
